answer: Identity Drift Penalty The protocol verifies each agent’s kernel state at every block to trigger the enforcement rule. A legitimate identity’s vine of stored hash forks naturally as it processes the distributed workload. An attacker’s identical clones share the same underlying state, forcing their karst cache entries to remain identical. The system freezes any account whose commit log matches another without required variance. The attacker pays the sum of all voided transaction fees plus the full collateral block attached to the duplicate identity.
